cond_0001.intro: The University Senior Financial Analyst is responsible for providing advanced and complex accounting and financial analyses for [Company name masked] in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Federal and State statutory regulations for all University financial matters. The University Senior Financial Analyst serves as a subject matter expert, providing sound and relevant analysis University-wide and at the unit levels to achieve both tactical and strategic objectives. They are charged with taking the lead on development management/cabinet level reports and will be the person responsible for the other Financial Reporting analysts.
cond_0001.responsibilities:
Regularly lead highly complex accounting assignments that are of diverse scope requiring analysis of identifiable factors using accounting and financial sources, including debt, leases, net assets, trusts, endowments, and investments for both University-wide and unit levels.
Develop audit schedules in coordination with the University's external auditors and assist in the preparation of all University financial statements.
Prepare tax analysis in coordination with the University's tax counsel and assist in the preparation of the University's tax returns.
Responsible for monitoring compliance with internal and external policies.
Prepares special external reports to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.
Demonstrate independent judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining solutions, completing analysis, and developing recommendations.
Lead development of financial reporting dashboards, reports, and visualizations for use by the Board of Regents, President, Cabinet, Deans, and Budget Directors. This requires a deep understanding of the interdependencies of modules and the skill to create formulaic analysis. This effort includes the determination of how to optimally convey information through the creation of charts, tables, summaries, and other presentation materials including dynamic and interactive materials.
Interact with senior internal and external contacts on matters of significance to the accounting and compliance of the organization.
Work with Budget Directors of the Divisions and Schools to help them understand key accounting policies and standards, as well as a chart of account hierarchical coding, to reflect accurate transactions for all funds (including current, designated, gifts, endowments, projects, etc.) while partnering to improve efficiencies and completeness.
Lead assignments where analysis of data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and multiple sources of accounting and finance-related data such as quarterly financial statements and ratios used by executive management for University planning and decision-making.
Determine methods and procedures on new assignments (new tax laws, accounting standards, and compliance requirements).
Interpret complex reports and records for administrators and directors.
Responsible for coordinating the collection of information, preparing summary schedules, and responding to inquiries from departments of coordinating resolution of issues involving other departments or functions.
Oversee the training and cross-training of other analysts, accountants, and interns on day-to-day functions in their areas of responsibility and consult with them when assigned ad hoc projects as to consistent and appropriate methods for data gathering, calculations and presentation in order to provide effective back-up support and guidance as needed.
Apply advanced accounting concepts to perform highly complex technical analysis to understand past performance, and determine present and future performance and/or resource allocations.
Prepare journal entries and maintain and/or reconcile complex general ledger accounts.
Maintain a system of internal controls over financial reporting transactions.
Assist in the maintenance of the unit's website and ensure Financial Reporting resource documents are kept current.
Stay current with accounting principles, trends, and industry standards for financial reporting and provide recommendations to senior management related to ongoing enhancements of University accounting policies.
Perform various tests of new functionality within the different enterprise systems used for financial transactions and make recommendations to improve financial systems.
Perform duties of the Financial Reporting Director and Associate Director in their absence.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.
cond_0001.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
Seven (7) years of experience in accounting and applying accounting principles.
Expert working knowledge of accounting regulations and all federal and state laws pertaining to financial reporting.
Advanced skills in MS Excel and other data systems.
Excellent analytical and quantitative skills to develop analytical, business reports and metrics including data mining, querying/accessing and summarizing large data sets.
Strong organizational skills and attention to accuracy and detail.
Strong ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Demonstrated ability to take primary responsibility for diverse number of tasks and complete them in a timely manner with limited supervision.
Demonstrates strong ability in analyzing complex issues and developing solutions and recommendations.
Must demonstrate the highest standard for ethics, integrity and confidentiality.
Strong communication skills and be able to communicate with all levels of the organization.
Experience and sensitivity in working with people of diverse backgrounds and cultures.
Preferred Requirements
MBA or CPA license.
Experience in higher education and/or nonprofit organizations.
Extensive experience with various analytic software tools and accounting systems.
Knowledge of college and university accounting or other not-for-profit accounting.
Physical Requirements
The physical demands described here are representative but not definitive of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Work is primarily performed in a standard office environment with use of computer, phone and office equipment. Requires extended periods of sitting and repetitive hand/wrist motion while using computer keyboard and phone. Occasional standing, walking, climbing stairs, bending, stooping and reaching. Occasional lifting up to 25 pounds.

cond_0070.intro: The University Senior Financial Analyst is responsible for providing advanced and complex accounting and financial analyses for [Company name masked] in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Federal and State statutory regulations for all University financial matters. The University Senior Financial Analyst serves as a subject matter expert, providing sound and relevant analysis University-wide and at the unit levels to achieve both tactical and strategic objectives. They are charged with taking the lead on development management/cabinet level reports and will be the person responsible for the other Financial Reporting analysts.
cond_0070.responsibilities:
Regularly lead highly complex accounting assignments that are of diverse scope requiring analysis of identifiable factors using accounting and financial sources, including debt, leases, net assets, trusts, endowments, and investments for both University-wide and unit levels.
Develop audit schedules in coordination with the University's external auditors and assist in the preparation of all University financial statements.
Prepare tax analysis in coordination with the University's tax counsel and assist in the preparation of the University's tax returns.
Responsible for monitoring compliance with internal and external policies.
Prepares special external reports to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.
Demonstrate independent judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining solutions, completing analysis, and developing recommendations.
Lead development of financial reporting dashboards, reports, and visualizations for use by the Board of Regents, President, Cabinet, Deans, and Budget Directors. This requires a deep understanding of the interdependencies of modules and the skill to create formulaic analysis. This effort includes the determination of how to optimally convey information through the creation of charts, tables, summaries, and other presentation materials including dynamic and interactive materials.
Interface with senior internal and external contacts on matters of significance to the accounting and compliance of the organization.
Coordinate with Budget Directors of the Divisions and Schools to support their understanding of key accounting policies and standards, as well as chart of account hierarchical coding, to reflect accurate transactions for all funds (including current, designated, gifts, endowments, projects, etc.) while working to improve efficiencies and completeness.
Lead assignments where analysis of data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and multiple sources of accounting and finance-related data such as quarterly financial statements and ratios used by executive management for University planning and decision-making.
Determine methods and procedures on new assignments (new tax laws, accounting standards, and compliance requirements).
Interpret complex reports and records for administrators and directors.
Responsible for coordinating the collection of information, preparing summary schedules, and responding to inquiries from departments or coordinating resolution of issues involving other departments or functions.
Oversee the training and cross-training of other analysts, accountants, and interns on day-to-day functions in their areas of responsibility and consult with them when assigned ad hoc projects as to consistent and appropriate methods for data gathering, calculations and presentation in order to provide effective back-up support and guidance.
Apply advanced accounting concepts to perform highly complex technical analysis to understand past performance, and determine present and future performance and/or resource allocations.
Prepare journal entries and maintain and/or reconcile complex general ledger accounts.
Maintain a system of internal controls over financial reporting transactions.
Assist in the maintenance of the unit's website and ensure Financial Reporting resource documents are kept current.
Stay current with accounting principles, trends, and industry standards for financial reporting and provide recommendations to senior management related to ongoing enhancements of University accounting policies.
Perform various tests of new functionality within the different enterprise systems used for financial transactions and make recommendations to improve financial systems.
Perform duties of the Financial Reporting Director and Associate Director in their absence.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.
cond_0070.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
Seven (7) years of experience in accounting and applying accounting principles.
MBA or CPA license.
Experience in higher education and/or nonprofit organizations desirable.
Expert working knowledge of accounting regulations and all federal and state laws pertaining to financial reporting.
Extensive experience with various analytic software tools and accounting systems.
Advanced skills in MS Excel and other data systems.
Excellent analytical and quantitative skills to develop analytical, business reports and metrics including data mining, querying/accessing and summarizing large data sets.
Knowledge of college and university accounting or other not-for-profit accounting preferred.
Strong organizational skills and attention to accuracy and detail.
Strong ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Demonstrated ability to take primary responsibility for diverse number of tasks and complete them in a timely manner with limited supervision.
Demonstrates strong ability in analyzing complex issues and developing solutions and recommendations.
Must demonstrate the highest standard for ethics, integrity and confidentiality.
Strong written communication skills and ability to communicate clearly with all levels of the organization.
Experience and sensitivity in working with people of diverse backgrounds and cultures.
The physical demands described here are representative but not definitive of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Work is primarily performed in a standard office environment with use of computer, phone and office equipment. Requires extended periods of sitting and repetitive hand/wrist motion while using computer keyboard and phone. Occasional standing, walking, climbing stairs, bending, stooping and reaching. Occasional lifting up to 25 pounds.

The University Senior Financial Analyst serves as a subject matter expert, providing sound and relevant analysis University-wide and at the unit levels to achieve both tactical and strategic objectives. They are charged with taking the lead on development management/cabinet level reports and will be the person responsible for the other Financial Reporting analysts.
cond_0088.responsibilities:
Regularly lead highly complex accounting assignments that are of diverse scope requiring analysis of identifiable factors using accounting and financial sources, including debt, leases, net assets, trusts, endowments, and investments for both University-wide and unit levels.
Develop audit schedules in coordination with the University's external auditors and assist in the preparation of all University financial statements.
Prepare tax analysis in coordination with the University's tax counsel and assist in the preparation of the University's tax returns.
Responsible for monitoring compliance with internal and external policies.
Prepares special external reports to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.
Demonstrate independent judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining solutions, completing analysis, and developing recommendations.
Lead development of financial reporting dashboards, reports, and visualizations for use by the Board of Regents, President, Cabinet, Deans, and Budget Directors. This requires a deep understanding of the interdependencies of modules and the skill to create formulaic analysis. This effort includes the determination of how to optimally convey information through the creation of charts, tables, summaries, and other presentation materials including dynamic and interactive materials.
Interface with senior internal and external contacts on matters of significance to the accounting and compliance of the organization.
Coordinate with Budget Directors of the Divisions and Schools to support their understanding of key accounting policies and standards, as well as chart of account hierarchical coding, to reflect accurate transactions for all funds (including current, designated, gifts, endowments, projects, etc.) while working to improve efficiencies and completeness.
Lead assignments where analysis of data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and multiple sources of accounting and finance-related data such as quarterly financial statements and ratios used by executive management for University planning and decision-making.
Determine methods and procedures on new assignments (new tax laws, accounting standards, and compliance requirements).
Interpret complex reports and records for administrators and directors.
Responsible for coordinating the collection of information, preparing summary schedules, and responding to inquiries from departments or coordinating resolution of issues involving other departments or functions.
Oversee the training and cross-training of other analysts, accountants, and interns on day-to-day functions in their areas of responsibility and consult with them when assigned ad hoc projects as to consistent and appropriate methods for data gathering, calculations and presentation in order to provide effective back-up support and guidance.
Apply advanced accounting concepts to perform highly complex technical analysis to understand past performance, and determine present and future performance and/or resource allocations.
Prepare journal entries and maintain and/or reconcile complex general ledger accounts.
Maintain a system of internal controls over financial reporting transactions.
Assist in the maintenance of the unit's website and ensure Financial Reporting resource documents are kept current.
Stay current with accounting principles, trends, and industry standards for financial reporting and provide recommendations to senior management related to ongoing enhancements of University accounting policies.
Perform various tests of new functionality within the different enterprise systems used for financial transactions and make recommendations to improve financial systems.
Perform duties of the Financial Reporting Director and Associate Director in their absence.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.
cond_0088.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
Seven (7) years of experience in accounting and applying accounting principles.
MBA or CPA license.
Experience in higher education and/or nonprofit organizations desirable.
Expert working knowledge of accounting regulations and all federal and state laws pertaining to financial reporting.
Extensive experience with various analytic software tools and accounting systems.
Advanced skills in MS Excel and other data systems.
Excellent analytical and quantitative skills to develop analytical, business reports and metrics including data mining, querying/accessing and summarizing large data sets.
Knowledge of college and university accounting or other not-for-profit accounting preferred.
Strong organizational skills and attention to accuracy and detail.
Strong ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Demonstrated ability to take primary responsibility for diverse number of tasks and complete them in a timely manner with limited supervision.
Demonstrates strong ability in analyzing complex issues and developing solutions and recommendations.
Must demonstrate the highest standard for ethics, integrity and confidentiality.
Strong written communication skills and ability to communicate clearly with all levels of the organization.
Experience and sensitivity in working with people of diverse backgrounds and cultures.
The physical demands described here are representative but not definitive of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Work is primarily performed in a standard office environment with use of computer, phone and office equipment. Requires extended periods of sitting and repetitive hand/wrist motion while using computer keyboard and phone. Occasional standing, walking, climbing stairs, bending, stooping and reaching. Occasional lifting up to 25 pounds.

Interpret complex reports and records for administrators and directors.

cond_0155.intro: The University Senior Financial Analyst is responsible for providing advanced and complex accounting and financial analyses for [Company name masked] in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Federal and State statutory regulations for all University financial matters. The University Senior Financial Analyst serves as a subject matter expert, providing sound and relevant analysis University-wide and at the unit levels to achieve both tactical and strategic objectives. They are charged with taking the lead on development management/cabinet level reports and will be the person responsible for the other Financial Reporting analysts.
cond_0155.responsibilities:
Regularly lead highly complex accounting assignments that are of diverse scope requiring analysis of identifiable factors using accounting and financial sources, including debt, leases, net assets, trusts, endowments, and investments for both University-wide and unit levels.
Develop audit schedules in coordination with the University's external auditors and assist in the preparation of all University financial statements.
Prepare tax analysis in coordination with the University's tax counsel and assist in the preparation of the University's tax returns.
Responsible for monitoring compliance with internal and external policies.
Prepares special external reports to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.
Demonstrate independent judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining solutions, completing analysis, and developing recommendations.
Lead development of financial reporting dashboards, reports, and visualizations for use by the Board of Regents, President, Cabinet, Deans, and Budget Directors. This requires a deep understanding of the interdependencies of modules and the skill to create formulaic analysis. This effort includes the determination of how to optimally convey information through the creation of charts, tables, summaries, and other presentation materials including dynamic and interactive materials.
Interact with senior internal and external contacts on matters of significance to the accounting and compliance of the organization.
Work with Budget Directors of the Divisions and Schools to help them understand key accounting policies and standards, as well as a chart of account hierarchical coding, to reflect accurate transactions for all funds (including current, designated, gifts, endowments, projects, etc.) while partnering to improve efficiencies and completeness.
Lead assignments where analysis of data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and multiple sources of accounting and finance-related data such as quarterly financial statements and ratios used by executive management for University planning and decision-making.
Determine methods and procedures on new assignments (new tax laws, accounting standards, and compliance requirements).
Interpret complex reports and records for administrators and directors.
Responsible for coordinating the collection of information, preparing summary schedules, and responding to inquiries from departments of coordinating resolution of issues involving other departments or functions.
Oversee the training and cross-training of other analysts, accountants, and interns on day-to-day functions in their areas of responsibility and consult with them when assigned ad hoc projects as to consistent and appropriate methods for data gathering, calculations and presentation in order to provide effective back-up support and guidance as needed.
Apply advanced accounting concepts to perform highly complex technical analysis to understand past performance, and determine present and future performance and/or resource allocations.
Prepare journal entries and maintain and/or reconcile complex general ledger accounts.
Maintain a system of internal controls over financial reporting transactions.
Assist in the maintenance of the unit's website and ensure Financial Reporting resource documents are kept current.
Stay current with accounting principles, trends, and industry standards for financial reporting and provide recommendations to senior management related to ongoing enhancements of University accounting policies.
Perform various tests of new functionality within the different enterprise systems used for financial transactions and make recommendations to improve financial systems.
Perform duties of the Financial Reporting Director and Associate Director in their absence.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.
cond_0155.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field required; advanced degree (MBA or CPA license) strongly preferred.
Minimum 7 years of demonstrated expertise in accounting and applying accounting principles.
Experience in higher education and/or nonprofit organizations desirable.
Advanced knowledge of accounting regulations and all federal and state laws pertaining to financial reporting.
Extensive expertise with various analytic software tools and accounting systems.
Deep proficiency in MS Excel and other data systems.
Exceptional analytical and quantitative skills to develop analytical, business reports and metrics including data mining, querying/accessing and summarizing large data sets.
Solid understanding of college and university accounting or other not-for-profit accounting preferred.
Strong organizational skills and attention to accuracy and detail.
Proven ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Demonstrated ability to take primary responsibility for a diverse number of tasks and complete them in a timely manner with limited supervision.
Proven track record in analyzing complex issues and developing solutions and recommendations.
Must demonstrate the highest standard for ethics, integrity and confidentiality.
Exceptional communication skills with the ability to engage effectively at all levels of the organization.
Substantial experience and sensitivity in working with people of diverse backgrounds and cultures.
The physical demands described here are representative but not definitive of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Work is primarily performed in a standard office environment with use of computer, phone and office equipment. Requires extended periods of sitting and repetitive hand/wrist motion while using computer keyboard and phone. Occasional standing, walking, climbing stairs, bending, stooping and reaching. Occasional lifting up to 25 pounds.

Maintain a system of internal controls over financial reporting transactions.
Assist in the maintenance of the unit's website and ensure Financial Reporting resource documents are kept current.
Stay current with accounting principles, trends, and industry standards for financial reporting and provide recommendations to senior management related to ongoing enhancements of University accounting policies.
Perform various tests of new functionality within the different enterprise systems used for financial transactions and make recommendations to improve financial systems.
Perform duties of the Financial Reporting Director and Associate Director in their absence.

The University Senior Financial Analyst serves as a subject matter expert, providing sound and relevant analysis University-wide and at the unit levels to achieve both tactical and strategic objectives. They are charged with taking the lead on development management/cabinet level reports and will be the person responsible for the other Financial Reporting analysts. Most people become stronger in this kind of financial reporting and analysis work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
cond_0203.responsibilities:
Regularly lead highly complex accounting assignments that are of diverse scope requiring analysis of identifiable factors using accounting and financial sources, including debt, leases, net assets, trusts, endowments, and investments for both University-wide and unit levels.
Develop audit schedules in coordination with the University's external auditors and assist in the preparation of all University financial statements.
Prepare tax analysis in coordination with the University's tax counsel and assist in the preparation of the University's tax returns.
Responsible for monitoring compliance with internal and external policies.
Prepares special external reports to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.
Demonstrate independent judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining solutions, completing analysis, and developing recommendations.
Lead development of financial reporting dashboards, reports, and visualizations for use by the Board of Regents, President, Cabinet, Deans, and Budget Directors. This requires a deep understanding of the interdependencies of modules and the skill to create formulaic analysis. This effort includes the determination of how to optimally convey information through the creation of charts, tables, summaries, and other presentation materials including dynamic and interactive materials.
Interact with senior internal and external contacts on matters of significance to the accounting and compliance of the organization.
Work with Budget Directors of the Divisions and Schools to help them understand key accounting policies and standards, as well as a chart of account hierarchical coding, to reflect accurate transactions for all funds (including current, designated, gifts, endowments, projects, etc.) while partnering to improve efficiencies and completeness.
Lead assignments where analysis of data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and multiple sources of accounting and finance-related data such as quarterly financial statements and ratios used by executive management for University planning and decision-making.
Determine methods and procedures on new assignments (new tax laws, accounting standards, and compliance requirements).
Interpret complex reports and records for administrators and directors.
Responsible for coordinating the collection of information, preparing summary schedules, and responding to inquiries from departments of coordinating resolution of issues involving other departments or functions.
Oversee the training and cross-training of other analysts, accountants, and interns on day-to-day functions in their areas of responsibility and consult with them when assigned ad hoc projects as to consistent and appropriate methods for data gathering, calculations and presentation in order to provide effective back-up support and guidance as needed.
Apply advanced accounting concepts to perform highly complex technical analysis to understand past performance, and determine present and future performance and/or resource allocations.
Prepare journal entries and maintain and/or reconcile complex general ledger accounts.
Maintain a system of internal controls over financial reporting transactions.
Assist in the maintenance of the unit's website and ensure Financial Reporting resource documents are kept current.
Stay current with accounting principles, trends, and industry standards for financial reporting and provide recommendations to senior management related to ongoing enhancements of University accounting policies.
Perform various tests of new functionality within the different enterprise systems used for financial transactions and make recommendations to improve financial systems.
Perform duties of the Financial Reporting Director and Associate Director in their absence.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.
cond_0203.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
Seven (7) years of experience in accounting and applying accounting principles.
Expert working knowledge of accounting regulations and all federal and state laws pertaining to financial reporting.
Extensive experience with various analytic software tools and accounting systems.
Advanced skills in MS Excel and other data systems.
Excellent analytical and quantitative skills to develop analytical, business reports and metrics including data mining, querying/accessing and summarizing large data sets.
Strong organizational skills and attention to accuracy and detail.
Strong ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Demonstrated ability to take primary responsibility for diverse number of tasks and complete them in a timely manner with limited supervision.
Demonstrates strong ability in analyzing complex issues and developing solutions and recommendations.
Must demonstrate the highest standard for ethics, integrity and confidentiality.
Strong communication skills and be able to communicate with all levels of the organization.
Preferred Requirements
MBA or CPA license.
Experience in higher education and/or nonprofit organizations.
Knowledge of college and university accounting or other not-for-profit accounting.
Experience and sensitivity in working with people of diverse backgrounds and cultures.
Physical Requirements
The physical demands described here are representative but not definitive of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Work is primarily performed in a standard office environment with use of computer, phone and office equipment. Requires extended periods of sitting and repetitive hand/wrist motion while using computer keyboard and phone. Occasional standing, walking, climbing stairs, bending, stooping and reaching. Occasional lifting up to 25 pounds.

Develop audit schedules in coordination with the University's external auditors and assist in the preparation of all University financial statements.
Prepare tax analysis in coordination with the University's tax counsel and assist in the preparation of the University's tax returns.
Work with the team to monitor compliance with internal and external policies.
Prepare special external reports to help ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.
Apply independent judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining solutions, completing analysis, and developing recommendations.
Coordinate the development of financial reporting dashboards, reports, and visualizations for use by the Board of Regents, President, Cabinet, Deans, and Budget Directors. This requires a deep understanding of the interdependencies of modules and the skill to create formulaic analysis. This effort includes working with stakeholders to determine how to optimally convey information through the creation of charts, tables, summaries, and other presentation materials including dynamic and interactive materials.
Engage with senior internal and external contacts on matters of significance to the accounting and compliance of the organization.
Work with Budget Directors of the Divisions and Schools to help them understand key accounting policies and standards, as well as a chart of account hierarchical coding, to reflect accurate transactions for all funds (including current, designated, gifts, endowments, projects, etc.) while partnering to improve efficiencies and completeness.
Coordinate on assignments where analysis of data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and multiple sources of accounting and finance-related data such as quarterly financial statements and ratios used by executive management for University planning and decision-making.
Work with the team to determine methods and procedures on new assignments (new tax laws, accounting standards, and compliance requirements).
Interpret complex reports and records for administrators and directors.
Coordinate the collection of information, prepare summary schedules, and respond to inquiries from departments, supporting resolution of issues involving other departments or functions.
Support the training and cross-training of other analysts, accountants, and interns on day-to-day functions in their areas of responsibility and consult with them when assigned ad hoc projects as to consistent and appropriate methods for data gathering, calculations and presentation in order to provide effective back-up support and guidance as needed.
Apply advanced accounting concepts to perform highly complex technical analysis to understand past performance, and help determine present and future performance and/or resource allocations.
Prepare journal entries and maintain and/or reconcile complex general ledger accounts.
Help maintain a system of internal controls over financial reporting transactions.
Assist in the maintenance of the unit's website and ensure Financial Reporting resource documents are kept current.
Stay current with accounting principles, trends, and industry standards for financial reporting and share recommendations with senior management related to ongoing enhancements of University accounting policies.
Perform various tests of new functionality within the different enterprise systems used for financial transactions and share recommendations to improve financial systems.
Perform duties of the Financial Reporting Director and Associate Director in their absence.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.
cond_0216.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
Seven (7) years of experience in accounting and applying accounting principles.
MBA or CPA license.
Experience in higher education and/or nonprofit organizations desirable.
Expert working knowledge of accounting regulations and all federal and state laws pertaining to financial reporting.
Extensive experience with various analytic software tools and accounting systems.
Advanced skills in MS Excel and other data systems.
Excellent analytical and quantitative skills to develop analytical, business reports and metrics including data mining, querying/accessing and summarizing large data sets.
Knowledge of college and university accounting or other not-for-profit accounting preferred.
Strong organizational skills and attention to accuracy and detail.
Strong ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Demonstrated ability to take primary responsibility for diverse number of tasks and complete them in a timely manner with limited supervision.
Demonstrates strong ability in analyzing complex issues and developing solutions and recommendations.
Must demonstrate the highest standard for ethics, integrity and confidentiality.
Strong communication skills and be able to communicate with all levels of the organization.
Experience and sensitivity in working with people of diverse backgrounds and cultures.
The physical demands described here are representative but not definitive of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

cond_0222.intro: The University Senior Financial Analyst is responsible for providing advanced and complex accounting and financial analyses for [Company name masked] in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Federal and State statutory regulations for all University financial matters. The University Senior Financial Analyst serves as a subject matter expert, regularly engaging University-wide and at the unit levels to support both tactical and strategic objectives. They are charged with taking the lead on development management/cabinet level reports and will be the person responsible for the other Financial Reporting analysts.
cond_0222.responsibilities:
Regularly lead highly complex accounting assignments that are of diverse scope requiring analysis of identifiable factors using accounting and financial sources, including debt, leases, net assets, trusts, endowments, and investments for both University-wide and unit levels.
Develop audit schedules in close coordination with the University's external auditors and assist in the preparation of all University financial statements.
Prepare tax analysis in coordination with the University's tax counsel and assist in the preparation of the University's tax returns.
Responsible for monitoring compliance with internal and external policies.
Prepares special external reports to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.
Demonstrate independent judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining solutions, completing analysis, and developing recommendations.
Lead development of financial reporting dashboards, reports, and visualizations for use by the Board of Regents, President, Cabinet, Deans, and Budget Directors. This requires a deep understanding of the interdependencies of modules and the skill to create formulaic analysis. This effort includes the determination of how to optimally convey information through the creation of charts, tables, summaries, and other presentation materials including dynamic and interactive materials.
Actively engage with senior internal and external contacts on matters of significance to the accounting and compliance of the organization.
Work directly with Budget Directors of the Divisions and Schools to help them understand key accounting policies and standards, as well as a chart of account hierarchical coding, to reflect accurate transactions for all funds (including current, designated, gifts, endowments, projects, etc.) while partnering to improve efficiencies and completeness.
Lead assignments where analysis of data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and multiple sources of accounting and finance-related data such as quarterly financial statements and ratios used by executive management for University planning and decision-making.
Determine methods and procedures on new assignments (new tax laws, accounting standards, and compliance requirements).
Interpret complex reports and records and walk administrators and directors through findings clearly.
Responsible for coordinating the collection of information, preparing summary schedules, and responding to inquiries from departments and coordinating resolution of issues involving other departments or functions.
Oversee the training and cross-training of other analysts, accountants, and interns on day-to-day functions in their areas of responsibility and consult with them when assigned ad hoc projects as to consistent and appropriate methods for data gathering, calculations and presentation in order to provide effective back-up support and guidance as needed.
Apply advanced accounting concepts to perform highly complex technical analysis to understand past performance, and determine present and future performance and/or resource allocations.
Prepare journal entries and maintain and/or reconcile complex general ledger accounts.
Maintain a system of internal controls over financial reporting transactions.
Assist in the maintenance of the unit's website and ensure Financial Reporting resource documents are kept current.
Stay current with accounting principles, trends, and industry standards for financial reporting and bring recommendations to senior management related to ongoing enhancements of University accounting policies.
Perform various tests of new functionality within the different enterprise systems used for financial transactions and make recommendations to improve financial systems.
Perform duties of the Financial Reporting Director and Associate Director in their absence.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.
cond_0222.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
Seven (7) years of experience in accounting and applying accounting principles.
Expert working knowledge of accounting regulations and all federal and state laws pertaining to financial reporting.
Advanced skills in MS Excel and other data systems.
Excellent analytical and quantitative skills to develop analytical, business reports and metrics including data mining, querying/accessing and summarizing large data sets.
Strong organizational skills and attention to accuracy and detail.
Strong ability to work independently and collaboratively, including regular communication with colleagues and stakeholders at all levels of the organization.
Demonstrated ability to take primary responsibility for a diverse number of tasks and complete them in a timely manner with limited supervision.
Demonstrates strong ability in analyzing complex issues and developing solutions and recommendations.
Must demonstrate the highest standard for ethics, integrity and confidentiality.
Experience and sensitivity in working with people of diverse backgrounds and cultures.
Preferred Requirements
MBA or CPA license.
Experience in higher education and/or nonprofit organizations.
Extensive experience with various analytic software tools and accounting systems.
Knowledge of college and university accounting or other not-for-profit accounting.
Physical demands: work is primarily performed in a standard office environment with use of computer, phone and office equipment. Requires extended periods of sitting and repetitive hand/wrist motion while using computer keyboard and phone. Occasional standing, walking, climbing stairs, bending, stooping and reaching. Occasional lifting up to 25 pounds.

Prepare tax analysis in coordination with the University's tax counsel and assist in the preparation of the University's tax returns.

Prepare special external reports to help ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.

Apply advanced accounting concepts to perform highly complex technical analysis to understand past performance and help determine present and future performance and/or resource allocations.

cond_0358.intro: The University Senior Financial Analyst is responsible for providing advanced and complex accounting and financial analyses for [Company name masked] in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Federal and State statutory regulations for all University financial matters. The University Senior Financial Analyst serves as a subject matter expert, providing sound and relevant analysis University-wide and at the unit levels to achieve both tactical and strategic objectives. They are charged with taking the lead on development management/cabinet level reports and will be the person responsible for the other Financial Reporting analysts.
cond_0358.responsibilities:
Regularly lead highly complex accounting assignments that are of diverse scope requiring analysis of identifiable factors using accounting and financial sources, including debt, leases, net assets, trusts, endowments, and investments for both University-wide and unit levels.
Develop audit schedules in coordination with the University's external auditors and assist in the preparation of all University financial statements.
Prepare tax analysis in coordination with the University's tax counsel and assist in the preparation of the University's tax returns.
Responsible for monitoring compliance with internal and external policies.
Prepares special external reports to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.
Demonstrate independent judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining solutions, completing analysis, and developing recommendations.
Lead development of financial reporting dashboards, reports, and visualizations for use by the Board of Regents, President, Cabinet, Deans, and Budget Directors. This requires a deep understanding of the interdependencies of modules and the skill to create formulaic analysis. This effort includes the determination of how to optimally convey information through the creation of charts, tables, summaries, and other presentation materials including dynamic and interactive materials.
Interface with senior internal and external contacts on matters of significance to the accounting and compliance of the organization.
Coordinate with Budget Directors of the Divisions and Schools to support their understanding of key accounting policies and standards, as well as chart of account hierarchical coding, to reflect accurate transactions for all funds (including current, designated, gifts, endowments, projects, etc.) while working to improve efficiencies and completeness.
Lead assignments where analysis of data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and multiple sources of accounting and finance-related data such as quarterly financial statements and ratios used by executive management for University planning and decision-making.
Determine methods and procedures on new assignments (new tax laws, accounting standards, and compliance requirements).
Interpret complex reports and records for administrators and directors.
Responsible for coordinating the collection of information, preparing summary schedules, and responding to inquiries from departments or coordinating resolution of issues involving other departments or functions.
Oversee the training and cross-training of other analysts, accountants, and interns on day-to-day functions in their areas of responsibility and consult with them when assigned ad hoc projects as to consistent and appropriate methods for data gathering, calculations and presentation in order to provide effective back-up support and guidance.
Apply advanced accounting concepts to perform highly complex technical analysis to understand past performance, and determine present and future performance and/or resource allocations.
Prepare journal entries and maintain and/or reconcile complex general ledger accounts.
Maintain a system of internal controls over financial reporting transactions.
Assist in the maintenance of the unit's website and ensure Financial Reporting resource documents are kept current.
Stay current with accounting principles, trends, and industry standards for financial reporting and provide recommendations to senior management related to ongoing enhancements of University accounting policies.
Perform various tests of new functionality within the different enterprise systems used for financial transactions and make recommendations to improve financial systems.
Perform duties of the Financial Reporting Director and Associate Director in their absence.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.

cond_0375.intro: The University Senior Financial Analyst is responsible for providing advanced and complex accounting and financial analyses for [Company name masked] in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Federal and State statutory regulations for all University financial matters. This role serves as a subject matter expert, regularly engaging with staff and leadership University-wide and at the unit levels to support both tactical and strategic objectives. The analyst takes the lead on developing management/cabinet level reports and is the go-to person for the other Financial Reporting analysts.
cond_0375.responsibilities:
Regularly lead highly complex accounting assignments that are of diverse scope requiring analysis of identifiable factors using accounting and financial sources, including debt, leases, net assets, trusts, endowments, and investments for both University-wide and unit levels.
Develop audit schedules in close coordination with the University's external auditors and assist in the preparation of all University financial statements.
Prepare tax analysis in active coordination with the University's tax counsel and assist in the preparation of the University's tax returns.
Responsible for monitoring compliance with internal and external policies.
Prepares special external reports to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.
Demonstrate independent judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining solutions, completing analysis, and developing recommendations.
Lead development of financial reporting dashboards, reports, and visualizations for use by the Board of Regents, President, Cabinet, Deans, and Budget Directors. Walk stakeholders through the interdependencies of modules and the formulaic analysis behind them. This includes determining how to best convey information through charts, tables, summaries, and other presentation materials including dynamic and interactive materials.
Regularly interact with senior internal and external contacts on matters of significance to the accounting and compliance of the organization.
Work directly with Budget Directors of the Divisions and Schools to help them understand key accounting policies and standards, as well as chart of account hierarchical coding, to reflect accurate transactions for all funds (including current, designated, gifts, endowments, projects, etc.) while partnering to improve efficiencies and completeness.
Lead assignments where analysis of data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and multiple sources of accounting and finance-related data such as quarterly financial statements and ratios used by executive management for University planning and decision-making.
Determine methods and procedures on new assignments (new tax laws, accounting standards, and compliance requirements).
Interpret complex reports and records for administrators and directors, explaining findings clearly and handling questions as they arise.
Responsible for coordinating the collection of information, preparing summary schedules, and responding to inquiries from departments and coordinating resolution of issues involving other departments or functions.
Oversee the training and cross-training of other analysts, accountants, and interns on day-to-day functions in their areas of responsibility and consult with them on ad hoc projects to ensure consistent and appropriate methods for data gathering, calculations, and presentation in order to provide effective back-up support and guidance as needed.
Apply advanced accounting concepts to perform highly complex technical analysis to understand past performance, and determine present and future performance and/or resource allocations.
Prepare journal entries and maintain and/or reconcile complex general ledger accounts.
Maintain a system of internal controls over financial reporting transactions.
Assist in the maintenance of the unit's website and ensure Financial Reporting resource documents are kept current.
Stay current with accounting principles, trends, and industry standards for financial reporting and actively share recommendations with senior management related to ongoing enhancements of University accounting policies.
Perform various tests of new functionality within the different enterprise systems used for financial transactions and make recommendations to improve financial systems.
Perform duties of the Financial Reporting Director and Associate Director in their absence.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.
cond_0375.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
Seven (7) years of experience in accounting and applying accounting principles.
MBA or CPA license.
Experience in higher education and/or nonprofit organizations desirable.
Expert working knowledge of accounting regulations and all federal and state laws pertaining to financial reporting.
Extensive experience with various analytic software tools and accounting systems.
Advanced skills in MS Excel and other data systems.
Excellent analytical and quantitative skills to develop analytical, business reports and metrics including data mining, querying/accessing and summarizing large data sets.
Knowledge of college and university accounting or other not-for-profit accounting preferred.
Strong organizational skills and attention to accuracy and detail.
Strong ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Demonstrated ability to take primary responsibility for a diverse number of tasks and complete them in a timely manner with limited supervision.
Demonstrates strong ability in analyzing complex issues and developing solutions and recommendations.
Must demonstrate the highest standard for ethics, integrity and confidentiality.
Strong communication skills and be able to communicate with all levels of the organization.
Experience and sensitivity in working with people of diverse backgrounds and cultures.

cond_0375.values: We value achievement, high standards, and work that is carried out with real discipline. We believe strong organizations are defined by the quality of what they deliver.

cond_0437.intro: The University Senior Financial Analyst is responsible for providing advanced and complex accounting and financial analyses for [Company name masked] in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Federal and State statutory regulations for all University financial matters. The University Senior Financial Analyst serves as a subject matter expert, providing sound and relevant analysis University-wide and at the unit levels to achieve both tactical and strategic objectives. They are charged with taking the lead on development management/cabinet level reports and will be the person responsible for the other Financial Reporting analysts. Most people become stronger in this kind of financial reporting and analysis work over time as they build experience and learn from feedback.
cond_0437.responsibilities:
Regularly lead highly complex accounting assignments that are of diverse scope requiring analysis of identifiable factors using accounting and financial sources, including debt, leases, net assets, trusts, endowments, and investments for both University-wide and unit levels.
Develop audit schedules in coordination with the University's external auditors and assist in the preparation of all University financial statements.
Prepare tax analysis in coordination with the University's tax counsel and assist in the preparation of the University's tax returns.
Responsible for monitoring compliance with internal and external policies.
Prepares special external reports to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.
Demonstrate independent judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining solutions, completing analysis, and developing recommendations.
Lead development of financial reporting dashboards, reports, and visualizations for use by the Board of Regents, President, Cabinet, Deans, and Budget Directors. This requires a deep understanding of the interdependencies of modules and the skill to create formulaic analysis. This effort includes the determination of how to optimally convey information through the creation of charts, tables, summaries, and other presentation materials including dynamic and interactive materials.
Interact with senior internal and external contacts on matters of significance to the accounting and compliance of the organization.
Work with Budget Directors of the Divisions and Schools to help them understand key accounting policies and standards, as well as a chart of account hierarchical coding, to reflect accurate transactions for all funds (including current, designated, gifts, endowments, projects, etc.) while partnering to improve efficiencies and completeness.
Lead assignments where analysis of data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and multiple sources of accounting and finance-related data such as quarterly financial statements and ratios used by executive management for University planning and decision-making.
Determine methods and procedures on new assignments (new tax laws, accounting standards, and compliance requirements).
Interpret complex reports and records for administrators and directors.
Responsible for coordinating the collection of information, preparing summary schedules, and responding to inquiries from departments of coordinating resolution of issues involving other departments or functions.
Oversee the training and cross-training of other analysts, accountants, and interns on day-to-day functions in their areas of responsibility and consult with them when assigned ad hoc projects as to consistent and appropriate methods for data gathering, calculations and presentation in order to provide effective back-up support and guidance as needed.
Apply advanced accounting concepts to perform highly complex technical analysis to understand past performance, and determine present and future performance and/or resource allocations.
Prepare journal entries and maintain and/or reconcile complex general ledger accounts.
Maintain a system of internal controls over financial reporting transactions.
Assist in the maintenance of the unit's website and ensure Financial Reporting resource documents are kept current.
Stay current with accounting principles, trends, and industry standards for financial reporting and provide recommendations to senior management related to ongoing enhancements of University accounting policies.
Perform various tests of new functionality within the different enterprise systems used for financial transactions and make recommendations to improve financial systems.
Perform duties of the Financial Reporting Director and Associate Director in their absence.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.
cond_0437.requirements:
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
Seven (7) years of experience in accounting and applying accounting principles.
Expert working knowledge of accounting regulations and all federal and state laws pertaining to financial reporting.
Extensive experience with various analytic software tools and accounting systems.
Advanced skills in MS Excel and other data systems.
Excellent analytical and quantitative skills to develop analytical, business reports and metrics including data mining, querying/accessing and summarizing large data sets.
Strong organizational skills and attention to accuracy and detail.
Strong ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Demonstrated ability to take primary responsibility for diverse number of tasks and complete them in a timely manner with limited supervision.
Demonstrates strong ability in analyzing complex issues and developing solutions and recommendations.
Must demonstrate the highest standard for ethics, integrity and confidentiality.
Strong communication skills and be able to communicate with all levels of the organization.
Preferred Requirements
MBA or CPA license.
Experience in higher education and/or nonprofit organizations.
Knowledge of college and university accounting or other not-for-profit accounting.
Experience and sensitivity in working with people of diverse backgrounds and cultures.
Physical Requirements
The physical demands described here are representative but not definitive of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Work is primarily performed in a standard office environment with use of computer, phone and office equipment. Requires extended periods of sitting and repetitive hand/wrist motion while using computer keyboard and phone. Occasional standing, walking, climbing stairs, bending, stooping and reaching. Occasional lifting up to 25 pounds.

cond_0514.intro: The University Senior Financial Analyst is responsible for providing advanced and complex accounting and financial analyses for [Company name masked] in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Federal and State statutory regulations for all University financial matters. The University Senior Financial Analyst serves as a subject matter expert, providing sound and relevant analysis University-wide and at the unit levels to achieve both tactical and strategic objectives. They are charged with taking the lead on development management/cabinet level reports and will be the person responsible for the other Financial Reporting analysts.
cond_0514.responsibilities:
Regularly lead highly complex accounting assignments that are of diverse scope requiring analysis of identifiable factors using accounting and financial sources, including debt, leases, net assets, trusts, endowments, and investments for both University-wide and unit levels.
Develop audit schedules in coordination with the University's external auditors and assist in the preparation of all University financial statements.
Prepare tax analysis in coordination with the University's tax counsel and assist in the preparation of the University's tax returns.
Responsible for monitoring compliance with internal and external policies.
Prepares special external reports to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.
Demonstrate independent judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining solutions, completing analysis, and developing recommendations.
Lead development of financial reporting dashboards, reports, and visualizations for use by the Board of Regents, President, Cabinet, Deans, and Budget Directors. This requires a deep understanding of the interdependencies of modules and the skill to create formulaic analysis. This effort includes the determination of how to optimally convey information through the creation of charts, tables, summaries, and other presentation materials including dynamic and interactive materials.
Interact with senior internal and external contacts on matters of significance to the accounting and compliance of the organization.
Work with Budget Directors of the Divisions and Schools to help them understand key accounting policies and standards, as well as a chart of account hierarchical coding, to reflect accurate transactions for all funds (including current, designated, gifts, endowments, projects, etc.) while partnering to improve efficiencies and completeness.
Lead assignments where analysis of data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and multiple sources of accounting and finance-related data such as quarterly financial statements and ratios used by executive management for University planning and decision-making.
Determine methods and procedures on new assignments (new tax laws, accounting standards, and compliance requirements).
Interpret complex reports and records for administrators and directors.
Responsible for coordinating the collection of information, preparing summary schedules, and responding to inquiries from departments of coordinating resolution of issues involving other departments or functions.
Oversee the training and cross-training of other analysts, accountants, and interns on day-to-day functions in their areas of responsibility and consult with them when assigned ad hoc projects as to consistent and appropriate methods for data gathering, calculations and presentation in order to provide effective back-up support and guidance as needed.
Apply advanced accounting concepts to perform highly complex technical analysis to understand past performance, and determine present and future performance and/or resource allocations.
Prepare journal entries and maintain and/or reconcile complex general ledger accounts.
Maintain a system of internal controls over financial reporting transactions.
Assist in the maintenance of the unit's website and ensure Financial Reporting resource documents are kept current.
Stay current with accounting principles, trends, and industry standards for financial reporting and provide recommendations to senior management related to ongoing enhancements of University accounting policies.
Perform various tests of new functionality within the different enterprise systems used for financial transactions and make recommendations to improve financial systems.
Perform duties of the Financial Reporting Director and Associate Director in their absence.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.
cond_0514.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
Seven (7) years of experience in accounting and applying accounting principles.
MBA or CPA license.
Experience in higher education and/or nonprofit organizations desirable.
Expert working knowledge of accounting regulations and all federal and state laws pertaining to financial reporting.
Extensive experience with various analytic software tools and accounting systems.
Advanced skills in MS Excel and other data systems.
Excellent analytical and quantitative skills to develop analytical, business reports and metrics including data mining, querying/accessing and summarizing large data sets.
Knowledge of college and university accounting or other not-for-profit accounting preferred.
Strong organizational skills and attention to accuracy and detail.
Strong ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Demonstrated ability to take primary responsibility for diverse number of tasks and complete them in a timely manner with limited supervision.
Demonstrates strong ability in analyzing complex issues and developing solutions and recommendations.
Must demonstrate the highest standard for ethics, integrity and confidentiality.
Strong communication skills and be able to communicate with all levels of the organization.
Experience and sensitivity in working with people of diverse backgrounds and cultures.
The physical demands described here are representative but not definitive of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Work is primarily performed in a standard office environment with use of computer, phone and office equipment. Requires extended periods of sitting and repetitive hand/wrist motion while using computer keyboard and phone. Occasional standing, walking, climbing stairs, bending, stooping and reaching. Occasional lifting up to 25 pounds.

cond_0646.intro: The University Senior Financial Analyst is responsible for providing advanced and complex accounting and financial analyses for [Company name masked] in accordance with Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and Federal and State statutory regulations for all University financial matters. The University Senior Financial Analyst serves as a subject matter expert, providing sound and relevant analysis University-wide and at the unit levels to achieve both tactical and strategic objectives. They are charged with taking the lead on development management/cabinet level reports and will be the person responsible for the other Financial Reporting analysts.
cond_0646.responsibilities:
Regularly lead highly complex accounting assignments that are of diverse scope requiring analysis of identifiable factors using accounting and financial sources, including debt, leases, net assets, trusts, endowments, and investments for both University-wide and unit levels.
Develop audit schedules in coordination with the University's external auditors and assist in the preparation of all University financial statements.
Prepare tax analysis in coordination with the University's tax counsel and assist in the preparation of the University's tax returns.
Responsible for monitoring compliance with internal and external policies.
Prepares special external reports to ensure compliance with federal and state regulations.
Demonstrate independent judgment in selecting methods, techniques, and evaluation criteria for obtaining solutions, completing analysis, and developing recommendations.
Lead development of financial reporting dashboards, reports, and visualizations for use by the Board of Regents, President, Cabinet, Deans, and Budget Directors. This requires a deep understanding of the interdependencies of modules and the skill to create formulaic analysis. This effort includes the determination of how to optimally convey information through the creation of charts, tables, summaries, and other presentation materials including dynamic and interactive materials.
Interface with senior internal and external contacts on matters of significance to the accounting and compliance of the organization.
Coordinate with Budget Directors of the Divisions and Schools to support their understanding of key accounting policies and standards, as well as chart of account hierarchical coding, to reflect accurate transactions for all funds (including current, designated, gifts, endowments, projects, etc.) while working to improve efficiencies and completeness.
Lead assignments where analysis of data requires an in-depth evaluation of variable factors and multiple sources of accounting and finance-related data such as quarterly financial statements and ratios used by executive management for University planning and decision-making.
Determine methods and procedures on new assignments (new tax laws, accounting standards, and compliance requirements).
Interpret complex reports and records for administrators and directors.
Responsible for coordinating the collection of information, preparing summary schedules, and responding to inquiries from departments or coordinating resolution of issues involving other departments or functions.
Oversee the training and cross-training of other analysts, accountants, and interns on day-to-day functions in their areas of responsibility and consult with them when assigned ad hoc projects as to consistent and appropriate methods for data gathering, calculations and presentation in order to provide effective back-up support and guidance.
Apply advanced accounting concepts to perform highly complex technical analysis to understand past performance, and determine present and future performance and/or resource allocations.
Prepare journal entries and maintain and/or reconcile complex general ledger accounts.
Maintain a system of internal controls over financial reporting transactions.
Assist in the maintenance of the unit's website and ensure Financial Reporting resource documents are kept current.
Stay current with accounting principles, trends, and industry standards for financial reporting and provide recommendations to senior management related to ongoing enhancements of University accounting policies.
Perform various tests of new functionality within the different enterprise systems used for financial transactions and make recommendations to improve financial systems.
Perform duties of the Financial Reporting Director and Associate Director in their absence.
Perform other related duties as assigned or requested.
cond_0646.requirements:
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.
Seven (7) years of experience in accounting and applying accounting principles.
MBA or CPA license.
Experience in higher education and/or nonprofit organizations desirable.
Expert working knowledge of accounting regulations and all federal and state laws pertaining to financial reporting.
Extensive experience with various analytic software tools and accounting systems.
Advanced skills in MS Excel and other data systems.
Excellent analytical and quantitative skills to develop analytical, business reports and metrics including data mining, querying/accessing and summarizing large data sets.
Knowledge of college and university accounting or other not-for-profit accounting preferred.
Strong organizational skills and attention to accuracy and detail.
Strong ability to work independently and collaboratively.
Demonstrated ability to take primary responsibility for diverse number of tasks and complete them in a timely manner with limited supervision.
Demonstrates strong ability in analyzing complex issues and developing solutions and recommendations.
Must demonstrate the highest standard for ethics, integrity and confidentiality.
Strong written communication skills and ability to communicate clearly with all levels of the organization.
Experience and sensitivity in working with people of diverse backgrounds and cultures.
The physical demands described here are representative but not definitive of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Work is primarily performed in a standard office environment with use of computer, phone and office equipment. Requires extended periods of sitting and repetitive hand/wrist motion while using computer keyboard and phone. Occasional standing, walking, climbing stairs, bending, stooping and reaching. Occasional lifting up to 25 pounds.
